summary: st-test terminates orphan fixture processes before reusing a locked pool tree

rules.detail: After acquiring a pool tree's flock, st-test scans same-uid processes, excluding itself and its ancestor chain. Kernel exe or cwd evidence inside the tree authorizes termination; absolute argv operands are resolved with realpath, but argv-only references refuse reuse without signalling. Execution-backed targets remain tracked through pidfds even if their paths change: SIGTERM gets two seconds, then SIGKILL gets two more seconds. Any surviving target, new tree reference or cleanup error refuses reuse.

compatibility.detail: No API or wire changes. Linux orphan cleanup uses pidfds to avoid signalling reused process identities. Existing test guardian signal cleanup is unchanged.

downtime.detail: Applies on the next st-test run.

recovery.detail: Revert to restore the previous wait-for-processes behavior.
